aboutParishDesc1: The parish of Saint Michel was founded in 1963 and was one of the parishes of the Archdiocese of Kabgayi. On May 3, 1976, it was officially named Cathedral Parish.
aboutParishDesc2: Since its establishment, the parish has played a significant role in the spiritual and social development of the community, serving as a center of faith and religious activities.

communityDesc1: The Basic Christian Communities (BCCs) refer to a group of interconnected Catholic Christian groups operating within our parish. These communities form the foundation of our parish life, bringing families together in smaller groups for prayer, fellowship, and mutual support.
communityDesc2: Each Basic Christian Community (BCC) members meet regularly in members' homes. These gatherings provide opportunities for Bible sharing, prayer, and addressing the spiritual and material needs of the members.
communityDesc: We cultivate a warm and inclusive community where everyone feels a true sense of belonging, finds genuine support, and embarks on a meaningful journey of faith and personal growth.
parishCommitteeDesc1: The Parish Council serves as the primary advisory and decision-making body for Saint Michel Parish. Working closely with the Parish Priest, the committee helps guide the spiritual and administrative direction of our parish community.
parishCommitteeDesc2: Parish council members are selected by the Parish Priest among different Basic Christian Communities leaders, choirs leaders, liturgy support team leaders and Catholic action movement leaders and serve three-year terms. Once selected, they meet up for a general assembly called by the Parish Priest and elect leaders of different commissions.They represent the diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives of our parishioners.
parishCommitteeDesc3: Through prayer, discernment, and collaboration, the Parish Council helps ensure that our parish remains vibrant, faithful to Catholic teaching, and responsive to the needs of our community.

committeeResp2: Developing and implementing the parish strategic plan
committeeIntro: Our Parish Council members are dedicated parishioners who volunteer their time and talents to serve our community.

massScheduleDesc: At Saint Michael's Cathedral, four Masses are held in three languages: Kinyarwanda, French, and English.
sacramentsIntroDesc1: Sacraments are sacred signs instituted by Christ to give grace. Through the sacraments, we encounter Christ and receive His grace to help us live as His disciples.
sacramentsIntroDesc2: At Saint Michel Cathedral, we are committed to helping parishioners prepare for and celebrate the sacraments with reverence and joy.
sevenSacraments: The Seven Sacraments of the Catholic Church
sevenSacramentsDesc: The Catholic Church celebrates seven sacraments, which are divided into three categories: Sacraments of Initiation to christian life, Sacraments of Healing, and Sacraments of Service.
baptismDesc: Baptism is the first sacrament of initiation into the Catholic Church. Parents wishing to have their child baptized should contact the parish secretariate to schedule a baptism preparation class. Babies are baptised following the faith of their parents every fourth sunday of the month
baptismReq1: Parents of babies seeking for baptism must be registered members of the parish and must have received the sacrament of the Holy matrimony
baptismReq2: Children from 7 years of age can be registered by parents. They individually attend baptism preparation class
baptismReq3: Selection of godparents who meet Church requirements i.e having received the sacraments of initiation to christian life, being an exemplary christian and participating in church activities
firstHolyCommunionDesc: First Holy Communion is typically received by children in the second grade after completing a two-year preparation program through our Religious Education program.
confirmationDesc: Confirmation completes the sacraments of initiation. Our parish offers a comprehensive preparation program for teens and adults seeking this sacrament.
confirmationReq1: Baptism and First Holy Communion in the Catholic Church
confirmationReq3: Selection of a godparent who meets Church requirements
reconciliationDesc: The Sacrament of Reconciliation offers forgiveness of sins and reconciliation with God and the Church. Regular confession is encouraged for spiritual growth.
confessionSchedule: Confession sessions are conducted every tuesday and thursday after morning Mass
marriageDesc: Couples seeking the Sacrament of Marriage or Holy matrimony should contact the parish priest at least six months before their desired wedding date to begin the preparation process.
marriageReq1: At least one person must be a baptized Catholic
marriageReq4: Necessary documentation (baptismal card and recommendation from the basic christian community)
anointingOfSickDesc: This sacrament brings spiritual and physical strength during illness, especially before surgery or when seriously ill.
anointingOfSickReq1: Being seriously ill, facing surgery, or at advanced age
anointingOfSickReq2: Contact the parish secretariate or the neighboring basic christian community leader to arrange for a priest to administer the sacrament
holyOrdersDesc: Through the Sacrament of Holy Orders, seminarians are ordained as deacons, priests, or bishops to serve the Church through ministry of word, sacrament, and leadership.
holyOrdersReq1: Discernment of a vocation to the priesthood or diaconate
holyOrdersReq2: Application to and acceptance by a diocese or religious order
holyOrdersReq3: Completion of seminary formation and theological studies
sacramentalPreparationDesc: Preparing to receive a sacrament is an important time of spiritual growth through cathechism classes. Our parish offers preparation programs for each sacrament in Kinyarwanda, in French and in English.
upcomingClasses: For students catechism classes are matched with academic year. Catechism classes are conducted on week-ends. For adults, catechism classes are ongoing and are scheduled taking into consideration both their availability as well as the one of catechists.
firstSaturdayMonth: Every first Saturday of the month in the morning from 09:00 to 10:30 AM; there is a prayer and worship conducted for confirmed young christians in French as a way to keep the fire burning and fellowshipping
baptismPrepDesc: For parents with babies and young children under 3 years of age inquire for their baptism throughout the month.
sundaysAfterMass: Sundays after 07:00 AM Mass, catechism classes are conducted in Kinyarwanda
firstCommunionPrepDesc: Two-year program for children in grade 2.
confirmationPrep: Confirmation Preparation catechism classes are conducted on Saturday morning from 10:30 AM - 12:00 PM in French; 02:00PM- 04:00 PM in Kinyarwanda; and on Sunday after 07:00 AM Mass; then 10:30 AM- 12:00 PM in English
confirmationPrepDesc: For youth in grades 4-5 preparing for Confirmation.
byAppointment: Catechism for the preparation to the sacrament of Holy matrimony are conducted every tuesday evening from 05:30 PM- 07:30 PM
marriagePrepDesc: For engaged couples planning to marry in the Catholic Church.
sacramentalPrepContact: For more information about sacramental preparation, please contact Sr Christine UWIRINGIYIMANA; the Coordinator of catechism program.
